effort: Brake before a square corner and project cleanly into a planned 90-degree exit.
brief: E2 is the running corner task. Low quarter-turn landings teach controlled reorientation, a shuffle-to-backpedal corner changes gait, same-leg lateral hops address outside-leg acceptance, a bound-to-run exit links lateral force to forward travel, and a three-point start isolates diagonal projection.
marker: In E2, record whether the athlete lowers before the corner, redirects through 90 degrees without a fixed-knee twist and keeps the first two steps inside the exit corridor.
readiness: Confirm quarter-turn landing and same-leg lateral control at low height before increasing intent. Prior class was prescribed as consolidation; no actual recovery has been established.
space: E2/E3/E5 require a measured 8 m × 5 m clear bay including straight-ahead abort and exit-stopping corridors. Orient the 2 m exit plus 2.5 m stop along its long dimension. Jump/short-start tasks can be oriented along the 10 m lane; actual side clearance still needs verification.

drills.name: Quarter-Turn Jump to Stick — bilateral
drills.execution: Low two-foot jump, turn the whole body 90 degrees in flight and land on both feet for a 2 s hold.
drills.job: Reorient the feet and hips together rather than twisting the knee after contact.
drills.layout: A clear 3 m × 3 m landing/fall area; no height or distance target.
drills.difference: An in-flight bilateral body turn, absent from all previous drills.
drills.regress: Reduce turn angle and height within the same task if feet land misaligned; log the changed angle.
drills.exposure: 1 bilateral landing; body rotation is not a locomotor cut.

drills.name: 90-Degree Speed Cut
drills.execution: Run in 1.5 m at controlled speed, brake before the cone, redirect 90 degrees and accelerate 2 m; stop over 2.5 m.
drills.layout: Mark the incoming line, corner and outgoing line. Keep 2 m beyond the approach cone clear for an aborted turn and the full 4.5 m exit/stop clear.
drills.difference: A square running corner needs different momentum redirection from the previous 45-degree cut; direction is the deliberate training variable, not a renamed time trial.
drills.regress: Reduce incoming speed if the athlete reaches for the plant or rounds the corner uncontrollably.

drills.name: Shuffle-to-Backpedal Corner
drills.execution: Shuffle 1 m, brake, then backpedal 1.5 m without rotating to run; stop over a further 1.5 m.
drills.job: Find backward force after a lateral plant while preserving the facing needed for the next task.
drills.layout: An L route in the bay; short lateral incoming leg, backward exit along the long dimension, mirror sides separately.
drills.difference: Lateral entry changes to backward gait; earlier transitions ended in forward running or lateral shuffling.
drills.regress: Shorten backward steps if the athlete leans back or crosses the feet.

drills.name: Single-Leg Lateral Hop to Stick
drills.execution: Hop laterally away from the free leg no more than 0.3 m, land on the same leg and hold 2 s.
drills.job: Accept lateral momentum when the outside leg must remain the support leg.
drills.layout: Face across the lane so flight follows its length; leave 2 m beyond the target clear.
drills.difference: Same-leg lateral landing rather than the opposite-leg bound or sagittal/diagonal hop.
drills.regress: Shorten flight for pelvic drop, inward knee movement or free-foot touch.

drills.name: Lateral Bound to Forward Sprint
drills.execution: Make one short lateral bound within 0.4 m, land on the opposite leg and immediately run 2 m forward; stop over 2.5 m. No second hop.
drills.job: Use lateral landing force to create a perpendicular running exit.
drills.layout: Place the bound at the corner of the bay; outgoing run and stop follow its long dimension.
drills.difference: The bound landing becomes a running redirection rather than a static hold or return bound.
drills.regress: Reduce bound distance and exit intent if the landing requires a recovery hop.
drills.exposure: 1 unilateral landing, 1 flight-to-run redirection and 1 terminal locomotor stop.

drills.name: Three-Point Diagonal Start
drills.execution: Use one hand on the floor and a stable staggered stance aimed down a diagonal lane; push forward into 2 m acceleration, then stop over 3 m.
drills.job: Direct force from a stable low position along the chosen exit without an approach or a cut.
drills.layout: Orient the whole start/run/stop down a cleared 10 m lane; the diagonal is relative to initial torso orientation, not a demand to cross occupied lanes.
drills.difference: A hand-supported low start changes initial support and force projection; not the falling or standing crossover start.
drills.regress: Use a less crouched start if the hand or trunk position is uncomfortable; stop if hand support is unsuitable.
drills.exposure: 1 start and terminal stop; no incoming-momentum cut.

light.job: Control pelvis reorientation over the planted leg at the square corner.
Maintain foot-edge control under a lateral component of the 90-degree plant.

strength.job: Main frontal acceptance and push-back contribution to the square plant.
Lead-leg knee/hip strength for the first perpendicular running step.
Maintain hip-hinge force while keeping fatigue modest as the corner task changes.
Knee-flexor support supplies braking capacity without another dynamic squat.
Adductor strength supports the pelvis through the larger direction change.
Bent-knee ankle force supports the low corner position.

previous_review: Class 4 prescribed only two direction changes and reduced strength to six rounds/nine bouts. Actual completion and recovery remain unknown.
progression: The new corner and flight-to-run task increase directional complexity, so approach stays short and support strength retains the reduced Class 4 round count. A sharper angle is not permission for higher entry speed.
strength_progression: Keep the Class 4 reduced round counts and target reserve. Shift exercise order toward the lateral lunge without increasing sets or load.
audit: Kept the running cut early and limited each flight support to two attempts. Included both a straight abort path and final run-off. Flight-to-run redirections are identified separately from purely running cuts in the per-drill exposure notes.
next: Next class develops backward momentum and open turns with short routes; review actual backward-step competence and recovery first.

light_entries.name: Hip Airplane — supported
light_entries.execution: Bodyweight, hand support and slight hip hinge. Slowly open/close pelvis through a small owned arc without rolling the stance foot.
light_entries.rest: Keep easy; rest 30 s between legs.
light_entries.regress: Reduce arc or use more hand support if knee/foot rotates uncontrollably.
light_entries.job: Control pelvis reorientation over the planted leg at the square corner.

light_entries.name: Seated Band Ankle Eversion — self-anchored (proposed)
light_entries.execution: Sit securely, use the other foot to hold a light loop; turn the working forefoot slightly outward against tension, 2 s return, keep knee still.
light_entries.regress: Use less tension/range for toe gripping or whole-leg rotation.
light_entries.source: Proposed exact setup; no verified identifier
light_entries.alternative: Use instead of the band, gentle hand resistance at the outer forefoot with the same easy reps if a loop cannot be secured.
light_entries.job: Maintain foot-edge control under a lateral component of the 90-degree plant.

strength_entries.name: Lateral Lunge — goblet dumbbell
strength_entries.execution: step out, lower **2 s**, push back to the original stance; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs**.
strength_entries.regress: Keep the lunging foot grounded and knee aligned; sit into that hip without rotating away. Reduce width, depth or load for loss of control.
strength_entries.job: Main frontal acceptance and push-back contribution to the square plant.

strength_entries.name: Split Squat — two dumbbells, both feet on floor
strength_entries.execution: **3 s down**, smooth forceful rise; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs, 120 s between rounds**.
strength_entries.regress: Keep full front-foot pressure and knee travel aligned with the foot. Reduce load/range for heel lift, knee drift or trunk collapse.
strength_entries.job: Lead-leg knee/hip strength for the first perpendicular running step.

strength_entries.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; **2 s down**, purposeful hip extension; 2–3 RIR. Rest **120 s between working sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Maintain a softly bent, nearly constant knee angle, weights close and a controlled back position; stop lowering at the owned range.
strength_entries.job: Maintain hip-hinge force while keeping fatigue modest as the corner task changes.

strength_entries.name: Glute Bridge Iso Hold — long-lever hamstring variant
strength_entries.execution: bilateral. Heels farther from the hips than a standard bridge, knees still bent; bodyweight or a securely hand-held sandbag over the pelvis to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Try to pull the heels toward the body without sliding them; keep ribs down. Bring heels closer or remove load for cramp/lost height; stop for symptoms.
strength_entries.job: Knee-flexor support supplies braking capacity without another dynamic squat.

strength_entries.name: Copenhagen Side Plank — short lever
strength_entries.execution: top knee/lower thigh on a stable bench, lower leg clear. Rest **60 s between sides**. Use bodyweight; if already controlled and too easy, secure a small dumbbell at the upper hip with the upper hand to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Keep shoulder comfortable and pelvis level. Use light lower-foot assistance if needed; stop for groin/shoulder pain or loss of position.
strength_entries.alternative: If no suitable stable Copenhagen support fits, use instead floor side-lying hip adduction, upper foot on the floor in front, 1 × 8 per lower leg at 2–3 RIR with 60 s between sides; add a small hand-secured dumbbell above the inner knee only if needed and comfortable. Its preparation is 1 × 4 easy reps per leg instead of the hold ramps. This proposed replacement adds 16 dynamic working reps and removes 30 s of working holds; preparation adds 8 reps and removes 10 s of holds. Bouts are unchanged; allow up to 2 extra minutes.
strength_entries.job: Adductor strength supports the pelvis through the larger direction change.

strength_entries.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, dumbbells on thighs
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; knees near 90°, forefeet on floor, **1 s at top, 2 s lowering, quiet bottom reset**; 2–3 RIR. Rest **90 s between sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Secure the weights above the knees, maintain knee angle and repeatable heel rise. Reduce load if heel height falls or bouncing replaces muscle force.
strength_entries.alternative: For seated calf work, use a securely held sandbag instead of dumbbells when its shape and load fit better.
strength_entries.job: Bent-knee ankle force supports the low corner position.
